summary_hint: a data-vendor property report for the SUBJECT property — address, APN, current owner, type/units, assessed & AVM value, tax status — e.g. 'CoreLogic profile, 41 Oak St (subject), owner J. Rivera, SFR, assessed $520k, AVM $610k, taxes current.'

typed_core.name: document_title
typed_core.why: processor — distinguishes profile source/vendor

typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: identity — CORE; the data vendor (source independence)

typed_core.name: data_source
typed_core.why: identity/disambiguator — which dataset the values come from

typed_core.name: report_date
typed_core.why: identity — CORE; report as-of date, drives recency of every value below

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: identity — CORE; the subject property

typed_core.name: parcel_or_apn
typed_core.why: identity — CORE; the cross-document match key for the parcel

typed_core.name: legal_description
typed_core.why: disambiguator — confirms the APN resolves to the intended parcel

typed_core.name: owner_name
typed_core.why: identity — CORE; current owner (must match borrower for a refinance)

typed_core.name: owner_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — second current owner

typed_core.name: owner_count
typed_core.why: disambiguator — guards a bad owner-name split

typed_core.name: owner_mailing_address
typed_core.why: processor — owner mailing != subject address is an occupancy signal

typed_core.name: property_type
typed_core.why: identity/processor — CORE; SFR/condo/2-4 unit

typed_core.name: number_of_units
typed_core.why: processor — CORE; unit count affects financing treatment

typed_core.name: year_built
typed_core.why: processor — age of improvements

typed_core.name: gross_living_area
typed_core.why: processor — living area headline

typed_core.name: occupancy_or_homestead_status
typed_core.why: processor — owner-occupied/homestead flag

typed_core.name: total_assessed_value
typed_core.why: processor — assessed value
typed_core.prompt_hint: Prefer county/assessor value for total_assessed_value and the vendor AVM for automated_or_reported_value

typed_core.name: assessment_tax_year
typed_core.why: disambiguator — the year the assessed value belongs to

typed_core.name: annual_tax_amount
typed_core.why: processor — annual tax

typed_core.name: tax_status
typed_core.why: processor — paid/delinquent status (title/lien risk)

typed_core.name: automated_or_reported_value
typed_core.why: processor — AVM/estimated value (value sanity vs appraisal)
typed_core.prompt_hint: On the subject property, the AVM value is a cross-check against the appraised value — keep it distinct from total_assessed_value

typed_core.name: valuation_date
typed_core.why: disambiguator — the AVM value is meaningless without its as-of date

typed_core.name: flood_zone
typed_core.why: processor — flood-zone code (drives flood-insurance requirement on the subject)

typed_core.name: subject_property_indicator
typed_core.why: identity — CORE; classifies this as the SUBJECT property
typed_core.prompt_hint: subject_property_indicator is fixed TRUE for this class, but extract the printed indicator rather than assuming

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity — links the profile to the loan file

rejected.reason: nested object, no consumer; the title doc is authoritative on vesting

rejected.reason: property detail with no rule; the appraisal is the authoritative source for the subject

rejected.name: land_use_or_zoning
rejected.reason: no consumer here (appraisal carries zoning for the subject)

rejected.name: valuation_date_and_confidence (nested)
rejected.reason: flattened to valuation_date; confidence is a conclusion

rejected.reason: a data report is not executed

rejected.reason: not a standardized form; no consumer

encoding_variations: Assessed value vs AVM/market value are different numbers from different sources — assessment_tax_year and valuation_date disambiguate them
Owner names appear as persons or as an entity (LLC/trust); owner_count guards the split
Flood zone may be a FEMA zone letter ('X', 'AE') or prose; capture the code verbatim

open_questions.q: Overlap with the appraisal (004) and subject property note (028) — for the subject property, the appraisal is authoritative on characteristics and value.
options: keep this profile lean as a cross-check source
enrich it with beds/baths/GLA to feed a value-reconciliation rule
open_questions.recommendation: keep lean until such a rule exists

open_questions.q: Sales/transfer & lien nested lists — same as 086.
open_questions.recommendation: defer to catch-all until a consumer exists GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

notes: No rules read this document today (rule_count 0); there is no rule floor. Identical field logic to the non-subject profile (086), differing only in that subject_property_indicator is TRUE. Fields earn a place by identity, disambiguation, or processor use.
No restricted fields on this doc. Owner names and mailing address are standard sensitivity -> kept as identity fields, not registry PII. No _PII_FIELDS additions.

sales_and_transfer_history and mortgage_lien_or_recorded_document_summary genuinely repeat, but no rule consumes them and each nested list costs ~5 sites of plumbing. Left to the catch-all until a rule needs them.
